name: Choline salicylate/cetalkonium (oral gel)
className: Topical oral salicylate analgesic with quaternary ammonium antiseptic

formulations.label: Oral gel
formulations.strengths: Choline salicylate 8.714% w/w, cetalkonium chloride 0.010% w/w
formulations.note: All content comes from the current UK SPC (revised 28/08/2026, from MHRA Products). An older 2020 text of the same SPC, still shown on emc, is superseded and is not used (the 2026 text changed the peptic ulcer, pregnancy and breastfeeding advice). Salicylate is likely to be absorbed across the mouth lining; MHRA: chronic, excessive use can give systemic salicylate levels of at least therapeutic levels.

items.t: Relief of pain, discomfort and inflammation from mouth ulcers, cold sores, denture sore spots and sore spots from orthodontic devices; helps fight minor mouth infection and heal denture/orthodontic sores.

src.q: For the relief of pain, discomfort and inflammation caused by common mouth ulcers, cold sores, denture and sore spots
To help to fight minor mouth infection and aid healing of sore spots and ulcers due to dentures and orthodontic devices.

items.t: MHRA/CHM: topical oral products containing salicylate are contraindicated in those under 16 years; they are no longer indicated in under-16s for teething, orthodontic pain, cold sores or mouth ulcers.

src.q: CHM advised that any topical oral product that contains salicylate should be contraindicated in children younger than age 16 years
Topical oral salicylate gels are no longer indicated for people younger than 16 years for pain associated with infant teething, orthodontic devices, cold sores, or mouth ulcers.

items.t: Adults and children over 16: with a clean finger, massage about half an inch of gel onto the sore area, not more than once every 3 hours. Do not exceed the stated dose. No change needed in the elderly.

src.q: Using a clean finger massage approximately half an inch of the gel onto the sore area, not more than once every 3 hours.
Do not exceed the stated dose. If symptoms do not improve after 7 days seek medical advice
There is no indication that dosage need be modified in the elderly.

items.t: Denture irritation: apply and wait at least 30 minutes before putting the dentures back; do not put the gel on the dentures.

src.q: Apply and leave at least 30 minutes before reinsertion of the dentures. Do not apply this product directly to the dentures.

items.t: Not to be used in children and adolescents under 16 years (possible association between salicylates and Reye's syndrome, a very rare and potentially fatal brain and liver disease).

src.q: Not to be used in children and adolescents under the age of 16.
This is because there is a possible association between salicylates and Reye's syndrome when given to children.

items.t: Salicylate doses above 100 mg/day in the third trimester of pregnancy.

src.q: Salicylates and Acetylsalicylic acid: doses > 100 mg/day during the third trimester of pregnancy

items.t: Breastfeeding (SPC section 4.6): contraindicated.

src.q: Therefore, this product is contraindicated in breastfeeding.

items.t: Contains salicylate: should not be used with aspirin or other salicylates except under the direction of a doctor or dentist.

src.q: This product contains salicylate and should not be used with acetylsalicylic acid or other salicylates except under the direction of a doctor or dentist.

items.t: Use with caution in active or recurring peptic ulceration.

src.q: This product should be used with caution in patients with an active or recurring peptic ulceration.

items.t: Contains ethanol (may burn on damaged skin) and fragrance allergens (d-limonene, anisyl alcohol, linalool).

src.q: It may cause burning sensation on damaged skin.
d-Limonene, anisyl alcohol and linalool may cause allergic reactions.

items.t: Anticoagulants: salicylates may enhance their effect.

src.q: Salicylates may enhance the effect of anticoagulants and inhibit the action of uricosurics.

items.t: Uricosurics: salicylates may inhibit their action.

src.q: Salicylates may enhance the effect of anticoagulants and inhibit the action of uricosurics.

renal.note: The current UK SPC gives no renal advice; it states salicylic acid and metabolites are excreted mainly in the urine. No MHRA/SPS renal content found.

hepatic.note: The current UK SPC gives no hepatic advice. No MHRA/SPS hepatic content found.

items.t: Third trimester: salicylate doses above 100 mg/day are contraindicated (section 4.3). The SPC also says the gel should not be used in the last trimester (possible fetal cardiopulmonary and renal toxicity, prolonged bleeding, delayed labour).

items.t: First and second trimester: no clinical data; should not be used unless clearly necessary; if used, lowest dose for the shortest time.

src.q: There are no clinical data from the use of Bonjela during pregnancy.
should not be used unless clearly necessary. If used, the dose should be kept as low and duration of treatment as short as possible.

items.t: Salicylates pass into breast milk at low levels and may very rarely harm the infant, so the gel is contraindicated in breastfeeding.

src.q: Salicylates are excreted at low concentrations in breast milk and may adversely affect the infant in very rare cases.
Therefore, this product is contraindicated in breastfeeding.

items.t: No information on effects on fertility.

src.q: There is no information on the effects of topical oral choline salicylate and fertility.

items.t: Frequency not known (short-term OTC use): hypersensitivity; bronchospasm and asthma attacks in susceptible patients.

src.q: Not known Hypersensitivity
Salicylates may precipitate bronchospasm and induce asthma attacks in susceptible patients.

items.t: Salicylate toxicity if the dose is exceeded; poisoning usually with plasma levels above 350 mg/L. Give supportive care or salicylate-poisoning treatment (e.g. activated charcoal, urinary alkalinisation, haemodialysis in severe cases).

src.q: Salicylate poisoning is usually associated with plasma concentrations >350 mg/L (2.5 mmol/L).
This may include treatment like activated charcoal, urinary alkalinisation and in severe cases haemodialysis.
